title: Rapid-pivot hire strategy and week-one activation (People Ops playbook)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working playbook for 'rapid pivot' hires — situations where a team needs a high-skill headcount filled within a compressed timeline (7–21 days to offer accepted). Primary goal is to minimize time-to-offer while preserving signal quality and ramp success. This document combines an outreach & interview campaign, an interview rubric optimized for speed, and a week-one activation checklist so the new hire can contribute fast.

Use cases this covers:
- Unexpected departure for a mission-critical role (SRE, infra, platform)
- Executive-directed headcount add with tight launch date
- Short window to convert a top candidate before counteroffers

Principles (decision guardrails):
- Preserve assessment fidelity: no fewer than 3 independent assessment signals (resume + short takehome/work-sample + live interview probe).
- Minimize friction: 1 recruiter + 1 hiring manager point-of-contact; consolidated scheduling blocks; 24-hour decision cycles.
- Fast, empathetic candidate experience: clear timelines, transparent comp band, single-threaded communications.
- Early success focus: week-one deliverables should be designed to produce visible impact and confidence.

Campaign overview (7–21 day timeline):
Day 0: Role brief & priority calibration
- Hiring manager + recruiter 30m: confirm must-have skills, nice-to-have, compensation band, interviewers (min 3), and offer approver.
- Create scorecard (see rubric). Post LinkedIn and send targeted outreach.

Day 1–3: Screening and sourcing sprint
- Recruiter does 30–40 targeted outreaches/day; sourcer works parallel with 2–3 prioritized channels (1) targeted LinkedIn InMail, (2) alumni network, (3) friendly referrals + internal pipeline.
- Initial screen (30m) scheduled and completed within 48 hours. Recruiter screens for availability/interest, pay expectations, and basic bar.

Day 2–6: Take-home + live interviews
- Candidate receives a short (60–90 minute) take-home task due in 48 hours. Task focuses on the core skillset: small infra debugging or design mini-problem for engineers; 3 prompts for product/PM.
- While the take-home is in-flight, book two 45–60m back-to-back live interviews on day 3–6:
  1) Technical depth + troubleshooting (hiring manager or senior IC)
  2) Systems design / cross-team collaboration (peer or architect)
- Optional cultural fit / manager sync (20–30m) can be combined with offer-stage loop to save time.

Day 5–8: Decision & offer
- Interviewers submit scores within 12 hours using the compressed rubric below. Recruiter synthesizes feedback into a short decision memo and proposed comp.
- Manager approves and recruiter issues verbal offer the same day; written offer within 24 hours.

Interview rubric (compact — single page):
Scoring: 1–5 (1 = miss, 3 = meets, 5 = exceptional). We require at least two scores >=4 and no scores <=2 to progress to offer.
Evaluation axes (each 1–5):
- Core technical competence (depth in role-specific systems, e.g., distributed systems, deployment pipelines)
- Problem solving & debugging (how they approach unknowns; root cause reasoning)
- Design & architecture (tradeoffs, scalability, simplicity)
- Collaboration & communication (clarity with cross-functional partners)
- Autonomy & ramp potential (learning velocity, ownership propensity)
- Culture / values alignment (curiosity, humility, bias for action)

Redwood-specific probes (examples):
- "Walk me through a time you reduced token-serving latency in production. What instrumentation did you rely on? How did you validate the fix?"
- "I just gave you a failing tail latency incident — what logs/metrics do you check first? How do you triage?"
- Take-home prompt (engineer): "Given a small microservice that begins to regress at scale, identify 3 likely bottlenecks, propose measurable experiments, and write a short script or pseudocode that would help reproduce the hot path."

Quick decision cheat-sheet for hiring managers:
- If >=2 axes scored 4+ and none <=2 -> proceed to offer.
- If mixed scores, prioritize ramp potential + problem-solving over domain-specific syntax.
- Avoid no-go decisions based solely on surface-level differences (language, framework) if candidate shows clear systems sense and ownership.

Offer packaging (fast approvals):
- Recruiter prepares a standard deck with comp band, equity guideline, and key negotiation levers (start date flexibility, sign-on, relocation remote stipend). Keep a pre-approved hiring committee signatory list to eliminate delays.

Week-one activation (first 7 calendar days):
Goal: get the hire to ship a small, visible improvement or complete a cross-team knowledge pass. Prioritize low-friction tasks that produce measurable signals.
Pre-day 1 (HR + infra):
- Accounts & access requested at offer acceptance: email, slack, Google, ticketing, repo access, CI dashboards, observability read-only.
- Manager assigns a peer 'navigator' (buddy) for day-to-day help and scheduling.

Day 0 / Welcome:
- Welcome note + 90-minute orientation: people ops intro (30m), security & infra basics (30m), team standup + meet the pod (30m).
- Hardware: verify laptop, VPN, and that the dev environment builds locally by EOW.

Day 1–3: Quick wins & learning loop
- Day 1: Shadow runbook review (30–60m), join on-call handoff or incident postmortem readout (if relevant).
- Day 2: Small triaged ticket assigned: low-risk bugfix or doc improvement that exercises the critical path (monitoring, deployment, CI). Owner: manager + navigator. Deliverable: PR by Day 3.
- Day 3: 1:1 with manager to align 30/60/90 goals, discuss blockers, set first-week success metric (e.g., PR merged, runbook updated, a dashboard created).

Day 4–7: Visibility & cross-functional sync
- Present the week-one outcome in team demo (5–10 minutes).
- Set up recurring 1:1 cadence and identify first mentorship checkpoints.
- Confirm training plan for month 1 (access to internal trainings, codebase tour, ops rotation).

Manager checklist (pre-hire + week-one):
- Draft 30/60/90 with measurable outcomes before start
- Identify 2–3 onboarding tasks that yield visible impact
- Reserve time on calendar for structured shadowing and knowledge transfer
- Assign buddy and a single point-of-contact for HR/IT questions

Hiring metrics for rapid-pivot (what to track):
- Time-to-offer (target: <= 10 days for urgent roles)
- Time-to-accept (target: <= 3 days post-offer)
- First-week outcome score (binary: shipped PR / updated runbook / dashboard created)
- 30-day ramp check (manager rating of 1–5)
- Candidate NPS (post process survey)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Shortened process reduces signal -> Mitigation: require take-home + two live probes + independent reviewer.
- Risk: Hiring manager bandwidth blocks -> Mitigation: hire a short-term interview proxy (senior IC) and standardize the rubric.
- Risk: Offer negotiation delays -> Mitigation: pre-approve comp levers and get sign-off before final interview.

Operational templates (copy-paste snippets):
- Recruiter outreach message (targeted, 3 lines):
  "Hi [name], I manage platform at Redwood Inference. We have a short-window senior infra role focused on latency and runtime reliability — fast process (7–14d). Comp: [band]. Would you be open to a 20m intro call this week?"

- Take-home instructions header example:
  "Timebox: 90 minutes. We want to see your thought process more than perfect code. Deliverable: a short gist or README explaining your approach and one code snippet or pseudocode puzzle solution."

Open questions / To resolve:
- Should there be a dedicated rapid-hire interview panel of on-call interviewers to avoid manager scheduling conflicts? (pros/cons listed)
- Define exact comp approval threshold that allows offers without exec escalation.
- Decide whether to keep cultural interview as a separate loop for final-stage or fold into manager sync.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Maya: finalize rubric and recruiter outreach copy (due 2025-05-05).
- Ethan: spin up targeted LinkedIn campaign and update job post (due 2025-05-06).
- Sofia: draft offer template and pre-approval list for comp levers (due 2025-05-07).
- Priya: create a short new-hire checklist in HRIS and automate first-week reminders (due 2025-05-09).

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider small paid take-home for senior roles to increase completion rate and reduce noise.
- Build a rotating rapid-hire interview panel (2 people/week) to avoid fatigue.
- Keep the candidate experience highly transparent: update them daily during the short cycle.

Attachment ideas (placeholders):
- One-page rubric PDF (to standardize scoring)
- Sample take-home repo + test harness
- Manager 30/60/90 template

End of draft.
